### 📓 Docs Drift Check
⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files. Nothing else in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **1** changed package(s)).

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **137** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json f8178ffeceba053667353f86ec193f2152ad557c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `efea2a386ebdf342b72b82bbdc5693e20998aaee`
Local-runs: none

Face: CHANGELOG prose (`packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md`, the released `@objectstack/spec` 17.4.0 entry for `094b8fd`). Read: the net diff against `origin/main` @ `9b0de7de7` (one hunk, +3/−1, one file, one commit), card #18858 and its three served comments, the PR body and its one bot comment, the 39 check-runs on this head, and git/npm where a claim needed settling. Not read: the dispatch order or the ACCEPT comment's conclusions, which were re-derived here. Hidden card comments: the API's `comments` count (3) equals the served count (3); any earlier comment the API does not serve is treated as absent, and no judgment below rests on one — the card body alone carries the finding, its readings and the rule.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept set and public surface: **none moves.** The diff touches no schema, export, default, bound or refusal; it rewrites one prose paragraph and appends one italic paragraph inside one already-published CHANGELOG entry. The only thing that changes for a consumer is the text of `CHANGELOG.md` in the next `@objectstack/spec` tarball — the surface this text exists to correct. `Clause-②: no` is right.

Every factual claim the amended passage and the appended erratum make, checked against git and the published releases (not the PR body):

1. **"at `rest-server.ts:2071` when the entry was written" — right.** The changeset that `094b8fd` (2026-09-08 06:54:22Z, PR #16775) carried spells the `:2071` anchor and the "owed to a follow-up" clause verbatim. At `094b8fd`, `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:2071` is the line "The cap is deployment policy — `RestServerConfig.batch.maxBatchSize`" (wrapped onto :2072 "(1..1000, default 200)"), and it sits inside the docblock of `private enforceBatchSize(...)` at :2076. So the relocation from a line number to the symbol names the same docblock the sentence actually lived in, and "the sentence was true when written" holds for both the anchor and the "owed" clause (no fix existed yet).
2. **"`ec5db7b` rewrote `enforceBatchSize`'s docblock to call the cap embedder policy" — right.** `ec5db7b` = "docs(rest): the batch cap is embedder policy, not deployment policy (#16942)", landed 2026-09-08 18:05:22Z, touching exactly `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts` and `.changeset/rest-batch-cap-embedder-only-prose.md`. Its diff deletes "The cap is deployment policy — … the place that knows the deployment's configured value" and writes, quoted: "Reachability: EMBEDDER-ONLY (#15543, #16801). ⛔ It is NOT deployment policy — this docblock said exactly that until #16801, and no shipped boot path makes it true." The amended passage's "the follow-up in `packages/rest` is ec5db7b" is also consistent with the card (issue #16801, landed as commit `ec5db7b` via PR #16942).
3. **"eleven hours after this change" — right.** Committer dates: `094b8fd` 06:54:22Z, `ec5db7b` 18:05:22Z, delta 11h 11m. "This change" in an entry headed `- 094b8fd:` is unambiguous. For the record, the entry was compiled by `7e6337007f` "chore: version packages (#15334)" at 2026-09-09 03:18:39Z — 9h 13m after `ec5db7b` — so the "owed" sentence was already stale when `changeset version` published it, which is exactly what the erratum says ("paid before this entry was published") without overclaiming that it was true at compile time.
4. **"shipped in `@objectstack/rest` 17.4.0" and "the same release as this entry" — right.** `@objectstack/rest@17.4.0` and `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` both tag `7e6337007f`; `ec5db7b` and `094b8fd` are both ancestors of that commit and neither is an ancestor of the 17.3.0 tags (published 2026-09-04, before either landed). That same commit deletes `ec5db7b`'s changeset file, adds the `- ec5db7b:` entry under `## 17.4.0` in `packages/rest/CHANGELOG.md` (:2612 on `origin/main`, section header :2264) and adds the `094b8fd` entry under `## 17.4.0` / `### Patch Changes` in `packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` (:14893 / :17905 / entry :18459 on `origin/main`). npm `time`: spec 17.4.0 published 2026-09-09T03:57:51Z, rest 17.4.0 at 03:58:13Z. The dev's and the PR body's readings match.
5. **"The phrase does not occur in `packages/spec/src/api/rest-server.zod.ts`" (unchanged clause) — still right:** zero hits at `094b8fd` and at `origin/main`.
6. **"One passage above is corrected in place; the finding it records and everything else this entry published are unchanged" — right, byte-checked.** The diff is one hunk. With the `094b8fd` entry (`:18459` up to the next `- aedbaef:` entry) cut out of both files, `origin/main` and the head are byte-identical. Inside the entry, exactly one line (the batch-cap passage) is replaced and two lines are appended at the end of the entry, before `- aedbaef:` — a two-space blank continuation line and the erratum paragraph, both at the entry's own continuation indent. The two-space blank line is the file's compiled convention (the entry's existing blank lines carry it too); `git diff --check` flags it as trailing whitespace, no gate does, and `Lint & Repo Gates` is green.
7. **The new anchor resolves on `origin/main` — right.** `enforceBatchSize` is at `packages/rest/src/rest-server.ts:2457` with its docblock directly above it, still carrying "⛔ It is NOT deployment policy — this docblock said exactly that until #16801". The retired `:2071` on `origin/main` is JSDoc on `resolveRequestEnvironmentId`, as the card and PR body say. A symbol anchor cannot drift the way the line number did.
8. **Shape against the guardrail — satisfies it.** `AGENTS.md` § Documentation Guardrails, `packages/*/CHANGELOG.md` row: "amend that entry in a dedicated docs-only PR, ⛔ never an erratum in a later entry and never a rider on code changes." The correction is inside the 17.4.0 entry for `094b8fd` itself — the passage a reader greps `deployment policy` into is the passage that is corrected, and the dated note sits in that same entry, not in a later one. It is a dedicated docs-only PR: one file, one commit, `docs(spec):` title, labels `documentation` + `skip-changeset` + `size/xs`, no `.changeset/` file, no code. The wording reuses this file's own precedent rather than inventing a sixth: `origin/main` carries six `*Erratum, YYYY-MM-DD — …*` lines (four in this same 17.4.0 section, one each in 17.0.0 and 17.0.0-rc.1), five of them closing with `(Corrected after publication, #N.)`; the two 2026-09-18 batch-cap errata (same subject, #18740) end their entries and say how many passages above were corrected in place, which is the placement used here; "The sentence was true when written" is the 2026-09-12 erratum's own phrase. The card ruled only the "owed" clause and the `:2071` anchor falsified and said not to delete the note; the diff does exactly that and nothing more.
9. **One residual, judged acceptable, named so it is on record:** the amended passage keeps the entry's present tense — "it exists verbatim in the REST server: '…' in the `enforceBatchSize` docblock". On `origin/main` that docblock no longer contains the quoted sentence. The card scoped the entry's other sentences as not wrong (they record the tree `094b8fd` landed on), the passage's own last clause says `ec5db7b` "rewrote that docblock", and the erratum repeats it. A reader who greps `deployment policy` in the tarball lands here and is told in the same paragraph that the sentence was rewritten in the same release — the misleading claim about outstanding work, which is what the card filed, is gone. Not a defect in this diff.
10. Citations: the amended passage cites the correcting commit by sha (`ec5db7b`), the record's preferred provenance; the erratum's `#18858` matches the five precedent errata's `#N` suffix and names the filed card. `check:issue-citations` defers `**/CHANGELOG.md` by declaration, so this citation was not machine-judged; the card exists and is an issue.

Check-runs on this head: 39, all `completed`, none `failure`. The seven required contexts are `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. `Check Changeset` appears twice (one `skipped` on the labeled event, one `success` on the opened run) — the governing conclusion is `success`. The bot's Docs Drift Check comment is advisory and says only that a CHANGELOG path yields no doc anchor, which is expected for this face. Not a governed surface.

### ② Semver level

**No changeset owed; `skip-changeset` is the correct declaration.** The diff publishes no code from any released package — it hand-amends a compiled CHANGELOG, which ships only when `@objectstack/spec` next publishes (17.5.0 is current on npm; the corrected text reaches consumers with the release after it). A changeset here would be wrong in kind, not merely unnecessary: `changeset version` would compile it into a new entry under a later version, which is precisely the "erratum in a later entry" the guardrail forbids, and the card's own remedy says "⛔ no changeset". The label is on the PR, no `.changeset/*.md` is added, and `Check Changeset` concluded `success`. The PR body's `Clause-②: no` line is present as the second line of the body and is correct — no accept set widens or narrows. ADR-0087 registration is not engaged (no breaking changeset).

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions`: empty. `out_of_scope_findings`: empty. `deviations` (six), each answered:

1. *Hidden card comments.* Confirmed as absent to this review too; the API serves three comments (Claim, `os-dev-report`, ACCEPT) and its count field reads three. The dev verified the newest `Claim:` names its branch and posted no second claim — correct. Nothing in this verdict depends on an unserved comment.
2. *Attribution.* The commit `efea2a386e` ends with the model-free trailer pair `AGENTS.md` prescribes — the session trailer carrying `https://claude.ai/code/session_01JAhu8u8QfBvRjVZDox7CP9` and the bare `Co-authored-by: Claude` co-author trailer — and the PR body closes with the session-URL footer. `AGENTS.md` outranks the harness reminder here. Correct.
3. *Shallow-clone ancestry reading discarded.* Settled here instead: in this checkout `git merge-base --is-ancestor` answers yes for both `ec5db7b` and `094b8fd` against the `@objectstack/rest@17.4.0` and `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` tags (one commit, `7e6337007f`), and that commit consumes `ec5db7b`'s changeset file. The dev's choice to rest the claim on the rest CHANGELOG section and the npm tarballs was sound, and ancestry now agrees with it.
4. *Four dist-reading gates NOT MEASURED locally.* Answered by the head's check-runs: `Lint & Repo Gates` and `TypeScript Type Check` are `success` on `efea2a386e`, and a CHANGELOG edit moves no build input. Closed.
5. *Worktree cleanup.* Process note; no bearing on the diff. Acknowledged.
6. *PR-body wording slip ("six instances").* Measured on `origin/main`: six `*Erratum*` lines, five carrying the `(Corrected after publication, #N.)` suffix (seven occurrences of the suffix in the file in all, the other two being inline amendments in 17.3.0). The dev's own count is right and the body's phrasing is the slip. The PR body is not a shipped surface and the diff does not depend on it; cosmetic, left to the dispatching seat. Not escalated.

The dev's acceptance note on the entry's retained present tense is judged in ① item 9. Nothing is escalated to the maintainer.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-18858-spec-changelog-paid-followup`
Reviewed-by: `session_01JAhu8u8QfBvRjVZDox7CP9`

**VERDICT: PASS**
